## Trial `host-firewall-baseline-rhel7__jcXJqPU`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** node1 has a persistent firewalld firewall (public zone) that allows only SSH and TCP/8080 and rejects all other inbound traffic via a REJECT-by-default INPUT chain, confirmed by direct iptables rule inspection both before and after a real, verified reboot (boot_id changed 192f6cab...->70e5b34e...) with a confirmed outage and full post-reboot recovery of the same rule set. Live end-to-end traffic testing was attempted but invalidated by a self-curl/lo-interface artifact on this single-node topology; the executor correctly diagnosed and documented this rather than presenting misleading results. Minor hygiene deduction for leftover /tmp test-listener and reboot-log artifacts that were never cleaned up.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.650 | 0.850 | 18/4 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Enable a persistent (survives reload) firewalld service on node1
  - **Why:** firewalld 0.6.3-11 was already active and enabled before the task; the executor confirmed this baseline and preserved it, and used --permanent + --reload for the new rule so the config is written to disk, not just runtime.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a4f5d0882bb74f49`, `cmd-79d471a1a37d42ee`, `cmd-48fd40b108d44126`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Permit inbound SSH
  - **Why:** Public zone lists 'ssh' service both at runtime and in the permanent config, and the IN_public_allow chain shows an explicit ACCEPT for tcp dpt:22.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-79d471a1a37d42ee`, `cmd-c1b0b67988514920`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Permit inbound TCP/8080
  - **Why:** 8080/tcp was added with --permanent, firewalld reloaded, and both runtime and permanent zone listings plus the IN_public_allow iptables chain (ACCEPT tcp dpt:8080) confirm the port is open.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-48fd40b108d44126`, `cmd-c1b0b67988514920`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Reject unrelated inbound connections
  - **Why:** IN_public_allow only matches tcp/22 and tcp/8080; the INPUT chain terminates in REJECT --reject-with icmp-host-prohibited for anything unmatched. A live curl-based test to port 9999 was attempted but the traffic looped over lo (self-directed traffic to the node's own IP bypasses the eth0-scoped zone), so it did not exercise the real path; the executor identified this artifact via packet counters and fell back to direct rule/chain inspection, adequate for a single-node topology.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c1b0b67988514920`, `cmd-b7213cbb4be2422f`, `cmd-4faeb9c3098e4f93`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** Configuration survives reboot (persistence)
  - **Why:** A full bounded disruption cycle was captured: pre-restart boot_id 192f6cab... with firewalld running/enabled and ssh+8080 rules; a deferred reboot acknowledged before disconnect; a confirmed SSH-timeout outage; a new boot_id 70e5b34e... after recovery; and post-reboot verification that firewalld is active/enabled with the identical public-zone config (ssh + 8080/tcp) and the same REJECT-by-default INPUT chain. This matches the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c6f0753416ce40c8`, `cmd-228feee56e93434e`, `cmd-b33ee281c43d44f2`, `cmd-c0d27b9a3f1f45d6`, `cmd-436881bcc07c4ddf`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.650**. The executor's core firewall changes were minimal and appropriate (one --permanent --add-port plus --reload). The diagnostic test-listener exercise (python3 attempt, then python -m SimpleHTTPServer on 8080/9999) was a reasonable bounded troubleshooting step, and the listener processes were killed (cmd-f100573c2d2e48e8, cmd-e22328c7079544fd, confirmed empty by cmd-84d43255606b43f8). However, the associated artifact files (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9999.log, /tmp/http9999.pid) were never removed and are still present in the after_executor snapshot, along with /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot-scheduling trick. These are low-risk, non-security-relevant residue but represent incomplete cleanup of executor-created temporary state.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-d12e4f7d18a84277`, `cmd-f825c1286ed8444d`, `cmd-f100573c2d2e48e8`, `cmd-e22328c7079544fd`, `cmd-84d43255606b43f8`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- No genuine cross-host packet test of the firewall was possible since this is a single-node topology; correctness relies on iptables/firewalld rule inspection rather than observed external traffic.
- Leftover diagnostic files in /tmp (http8080.log/pid, http9999.log/pid, reboot.log) were not cleaned up after use, though they pose no functional or security risk.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.650); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
